keyPoints: Dilute acid: salt + hydrogen.
Cold water: metal hydroxide + hydrogen.
Steam: metal oxide + hydrogen.
Oxygen: metal oxide.
modelAnswer: Metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen; for example, Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2. Reactive metals react with cold water to form a metal hydroxide and hydrogen; for example, 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2. With steam, metals form a metal oxide and hydrogen; the chapter gives Mg + H2O(g) -> MgO + H2. With oxygen, metals form metal oxides; for example, 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO.

modelAnswer: The general properties are: with dilute acids, metals form a salt and hydrogen (for example Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2); with cold water, reactive metals form a hydroxide and hydrogen (2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2); with steam, metals form an oxide and hydrogen (Mg + H2O(g) -> MgO + H2); with oxygen, metals form metal oxides (2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO).
